reason: Section 75 contains two separate mining lease topics: the operational rights granted to the lessee and the holder liability for damage or interference on the lease area.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mining lease access, prospecting, mining and production rights
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 75(1) lists the rights a mining lease gives the lessee, including access, prospecting, mining, sampling, testing and production rights.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the access, prospecting, mining, sampling, testing and production rights granted by a mining lease.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mining lease holder liability for damage or interference
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 75(2) separately states the holder liability for actual damage to or interference with use and enjoyment of property.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the holder of a mining lease is liable for damage or interference with property use and enjoyment.

reason: Section 76 separates immediate notice duties when production misses, drops or ceases from the Minister’s ability to require in-Province processing and the economic-ability limit on that requirement.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Notice of delayed, reduced or ceased production
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 76(1) sets the production situations that trigger immediate notice to the Minister with reasons.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a lessee must immediately notify the Minister about production failure, reduction or cessation.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister-required mineral processing in the Province
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 76(2) and 76(3) work together because one authorizes a processing requirement and the other limits it to cases where the lessee is economically able.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Minister may require minerals mined under a lease to be processed or further processed in the Province.

reason: Section 77 is one opening or reopening workflow: advance notice and feasibility-study revisions must be submitted before production work begins, with approval required for environmental program revisions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Opening or reopening mine notice and pre-work approvals
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address the notice, revised feasibility particulars and approvals required before opening or reopening production work.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the notice, revised feasibility particulars and approvals required before opening or reopening a mine for production.

reason: Section 78 states the lessee’s paired environmental obligations to protect the environment during mining operations and reclaim or rehabilitate it to the Minister’s satisfaction.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Lessee environmental protection and reclamation obligations

evidenceText: institute and carry out a program for the protection of the environment
undertake and complete a program for the reclamation and rehabilitation

proposedGroups.reason: The target consists of two related obligations imposed on every lessee for environmental protection, reclamation and rehabilitation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the environmental protection, reclamation and rehabilitation programs every lessee must carry out.

reason: Section 79 is repeal-only and contains no current operative study content.
Section 80 is a focused reporting provision requiring lessees and lease holders to submit regulation-required returns and an annual work-and-minerals statement.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mining lease returns and annual work statement
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections concern returns or statements to the Recorder about work and minerals under a mining lease.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the returns and annual work-and-minerals statement required from lessees and mining lease holders.

reason: Section 81 gives one recurring statement duty tied to specified lease anniversaries and inspection of boundary lines.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Lease boundary-line inspection statement

evidenceText: fifth, tenth, fifteenth and twentieth anniversaries
boundary lines of the lease area have been inspected

proposedGroups.reason: The target is a single timing and content rule for a statement verifying inspection and visibility of lease boundary lines.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the lessee must submit a statement verifying inspection and visibility of lease boundary lines.

reason: Section 82 is a single pre-closing notice rule requiring written notice and any required plans or documents before closing, abandoning or making a mine inaccessible.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Notice before closing, abandoning or making a mine inaccessible

evidenceText: At least ninety days prior to closing or abandoning a mine
provide the Minister with such plans or other documents

proposedGroups.reason: The target states one advance-notice and document-production obligation before closing, abandoning or rendering a mine inaccessible.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the notice and document duties before closing, abandoning or rendering a mine inaccessible.

reason: Section 83 only identifies sections 70 to 82 as mining lease terms and conditions; the teachable content is in those referenced provisions rather than this target.
Section 84 contains one group of investigation and decision steps after alleged non-compliance, and a separate consequence group for cancellation and withdrawal of the lease land.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister notice, investigation and decision after lease non-compliance
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 84(1) and 84(2) set the notice, minimum investigation timing, investigation, possible lease cancellation or extensions, and notice of decision.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Minister’s notice, investigation and decision powers after alleged mining lease non-compliance.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Lease cancellation after extended non-compliance and land withdrawal
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 84(3) and 84(4) state the mandatory cancellation after failure to comply within extended time and the resulting withdrawal of land.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what happens when a lessee fails to comply within an extended time and how cancelled lease land is treated.

reason: Section 85 is one surrender-filing rule with a related substitute statement when the counterpart of the lease is lost or unavailable.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Surrender of mining lease and missing counterpart statement
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address how a lessee files a surrender and what may replace a lost or unavailable lease counterpart.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a lessee surrenders a mining lease and what replaces a lost or unavailable counterpart.

reason: Section 86 states one consequence of lease expiry or surrender: the covered land is withdrawn until the Recorder sets a time.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Land withdrawal after lease expiry or surrender

evidenceText: withdrawn from prospecting and registration of mineral claims

proposedGroups.reason: The target contains a single rule about withdrawal of land after a mining lease expires or is surrendered.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how land is treated after a mining lease expires or is surrendered.

reason: Section 87 separates the former lessee’s one-year removal rights and limits from ownership rules for remaining property and extracted minerals.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Former lessee one-year removal rights and limits
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 87(1) sets the one-year period for removing structures, equipment and minerals and identifies supports, timbers and framework that may not be removed.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what a former lessee may remove within one year after a lease expires, is surrendered or is cancelled.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Ownership of property and extracted minerals left after the removal period
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 87(2) and 87(3) state who owns remaining structures, equipment, property and extracted minerals after the removal period expires.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who owns structures, equipment, property and extracted minerals left after the former lessee’s removal period expires.

reason: Section 88 gives one continuing-liability rule for royalties, rents, reclamation, rehabilitation and other obligations after a lease expires, is surrendered or is cancelled.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Continuing liabilities after mining lease ends

evidenceText: continues to be liable for any money owing
reclamation and rehabilitation of the land

proposedGroups.reason: The target is a single rule preserving the former lessee’s liabilities after the lease ends.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which liabilities continue after a mining lease expires, is surrendered or is cancelled.

reason: Section 89 is one application-based power for the Minister to authorize changes to land covered by a mining lease on prescribed fee, good cause and terms and conditions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister authorization to change land covered by a mining lease
proposedGroups.reason: The target states the Minister’s power to authorize reduction, subdivision, amalgamation or enlargement of leased land.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how land covered by a mining lease may be reduced, subdivided, amalgamated or enlarged.

reason: Section 90 states who must carry out a boundary survey and that it must be carried out in accordance with the Surveys Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Boundary survey qualification and governing Act

evidenceText: by a land surveyor who is qualified
in accordance with the Surveys Act

proposedGroups.reason: The target is a single boundary-survey rule about qualified land surveyors and compliance with the Surveys Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who must carry out a boundary survey and the Act it must follow.

reason: Section 91 gives one technical boundary-survey rule for coordinate designation, orthometric heights, CGVD2013 and approved bench marks.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Boundary survey coordinates, heights and bench marks
proposedGroups.reason: The target is a single technical standard for angles and heights in boundary surveys.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how angles and orthometric heights in a boundary survey must be designated and derived.

reason: Section 92 states one precondition for a boundary survey: the surveyor must obtain an order of survey issued by the Minister.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Order of survey before boundary survey

evidenceText: Prior to carrying out a boundary survey
obtain an order of survey issued by the Minister

proposedGroups.reason: The target is a single rule requiring an order of survey before a boundary survey is carried out.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what a surveyor must obtain before carrying out a boundary survey.
